anticipated_bypass_text: We will utilize an empty primary clarifier (84,000 gallons) to contain the flow during a planned power outage.  We will back up flow in our facility collection system.  We will shut down pumping from our main lift station and back up flow in the collection system.  We will hold water back as long as possible during the power outage.  We will have the aeration tank as low as possible and shut down recycle flows.  If the flow crests the slide gate we will allow overflow to fill the aeration wet-well.  Once the wet-well is filled to over 11' ( 45,000 gallons) we are out of room and allow the water to bypass the secondary treatment and discharge to the Missouri River.

sewer_overflow_reporting_requirement_des: Anticipated bypass notice
anticipated_bypass_text: We will take down one of our primary clarifiers and will send flow into the empty clarifier to stop flow to the aeration wetwell.  We will shut down the pumps and drain the header back to the wetwell.  John T Jones construction along with RP constructors and Laser Edge concrete cutting will perform the work to remove the old pipe, core a larger hole to the aeration drywell, install the new ductile pipe and fittings along with a new in line flowmeter.  Once the primary clarifier is full and flow continues to the aeration wetwell we will use our EQ pump to pump all plant flow to our EQ containment lagoon.  This lagoon is empty and has a capacity of 1 million gallons and an extra overflow capacity to our water lagoon B of another 500,000 gallons.  This will stop all flow through the secondary treatment stage and we will not be discharging during this operation.  Once the pipe header is assembled we will start flow back through the secondary treatment system and resume normal discharge.
